prerequisites: CS-UH 1001 (Intro to Computer Science); corequisite CS-UH 1002 (Discrete Mathematics) — required, exam-tested prior/concurrent coursework, not optional background. No prior C++ is assumed, but prior general programming (from CS-UH 1001) is.
courseDescription: A required, cumulative 4-credit data structures & algorithms course taught in C++, textbook Goodrich/Tamassia/Mount 'Data Structures and Algorithms in C++' (2nd ed.). Every enrolled student is examined on the full syllabus; there is no elective/alternative-track content. AI-assisted code generation is explicitly disallowed by course policy (idea generation only).
assessmentMethods: 4 quizzes 15%, 3 assignments 20%, lab 10%, midterm exam 25%, final exam 30%. 55% of the grade is exam-based on material every student must know.
learningObjectives: Design appropriate data structures for a given problem
Analyze and compare algorithm performance using asymptotic (Big-O) notation
Demonstrate proficiency with standard data structures (lists, trees, heaps, hash tables)
Design and implement efficient programs using the structures covered

blocks.title: C++ Foundations & Object-Oriented Design
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — the one block where prior-C++-exposure most changes needed scaffolding; students with no prior C++ get extra scaffolding nodes here, students with strong prior C++ get enrichment nodes (e.g. move semantics, templates depth) instead.
objectives: Write and compile basic C++ programs (references, arrays, classes)
Apply object-oriented design: inheritance, templates, exceptions

blocks.title: Arrays, Linked Lists & Recursion
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block; includes Quiz 1 (recursion) as an assessment checkpoint.

blocks.title: Stacks, Queues & Sequence-Based Structures
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block; includes Quiz 2 and a midterm-review assessment checkpoint (material through this block is on the midterm).
objectives: Implement vectors, iterators, and lists; apply bubble sort

blocks.title: Trees & Tree Traversal
objectives: Implement general trees and binary trees

blocks.title: Priority Queues & Heaps
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — smaller than others by lesson count, floor should scale down proportionally, not disappear.

blocks.title: Maps, Hash Tables & Dictionaries
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block; includes Quiz 3 as an assessment checkpoint.
objectives: Compare hash functions, skip lists, ordered maps, and dictionaries

lessons.title: Hash Functions, Skip Lists, Ordered Maps & Dictionaries

blocks.title: Balanced & Search Trees (BST, AVL, Red-Black)
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — the most theory/proof-heavy block; students weaker in discrete-math/proof reasoning get extra scaffolding here.
objectives: Compare AVL, multi-way search, (2,4), and red-black trees

blocks.title: Sorting Algorithms & Course Capstone
blocks.pathwayNote: Required capstone block; includes Quiz 4 and the cumulative final-exam review checkpoint.
objectives: Implement and compare merge sort and selection sort
Synthesize the full course's data structures for the cumulative final
